title: fix(console): an injected spec shares the console's one zod instance (objectui#11327)
body:
Fixes #11327

## What this does

Under `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` (the framework's `scripts/build-console.sh`), the console bundle now carries exactly ONE zod instance. The maintainer's ruling asked for one instance, not two copies that happen to agree.

- **`pinZodToConsoleCopy`** (in `scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts`, returned on the injection as `singleZodPlugin`): a pre-resolver (`enforce: 'pre'`, hook filter on `^zod(/|$)`). It resolves every bare `zod` / `zod/...` specifier through the rest of the resolver chain as if `packages/app-shell` had imported it. That includes the imports in the injected spec's out-of-tree files. Exports-map subpaths and the import kind are still honoured; the only thing that changes is which install tree the lookup happens in. The build fails by name if a specifier stops resolving from the anchor, or resolves outside the anchor's zod.
- **`assertSpecZodParity`** (runs inside `resolveSpecDistInjection`, beside `assertSpecDependenciesResolve`): the build fails when the console's zod does not satisfy the `zod` range the injected spec declares in `dependencies` or `peerDependencies`. The error names both. The range reader `versionSatisfiesRange` is deliberately narrow and throws on any spelling it cannot read, the same trade `minVersionOf` makes in `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs`.
- **`assertSingleZodInstance`** (wired into every console build, injected or not): counts the zod package directories rendered into the emitted chunks. It fails on more than one, and the message names each copy's version, path, chunks and importers. Two copies of the same version also fail, because the guard counts instances, not versions. It also fails on zero, as a counter-probe, because a negative guard that cannot see zod would stay green forever.
- `consoleZodFrom` is a **required** option of `resolveSpecDistInjection`, so a caller cannot forget it.
- `apps/console/vite.config.ts` passes `CONSOLE_ZOD_ANCHOR` (`packages/app-shell`, the package whose metadata-admin `*-schema.ts` modules call `z.toJSONSchema` over spec schemas, and which declares `zod` itself). It registers the redirect only while the override is live and registers the guard always. A comment next to `resolve.dedupe` records why `zod` is not listed there.

## Why not `resolve.dedupe` (the suggested route, measured and rejected)

Vite resolves a deduped package from the **root**. The console root (`apps/console`) declares no `zod`, so that lookup finds nothing and Vite silently falls back to the importer's own copy. I measured this with `zod` added to `dedupe` on the real console config, using `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` and `OBJECTSTACK_CLIENT_DIST` pointed at a built `/home/user/objectstack` (`ef1ed17f`). The build emitted the same two copies, and the `vendor-objectstack` asset hash was byte-identical to the build without dedupe (`vendor-objectstack-B_ZeTkdj.js` in both). A scratch Vite 8.2.2 project showed the mechanism directly: dedupe does reach out-of-root importers, but only when the root itself can resolve the package. When it can't, there is no warning.

## Measurements (objectui `5262f7dd3` base; framework `ef1ed17f`, spec 17.5.0 declares `zod ^4.6.1`)

The figures below come from counting distinct zod version-object literals and `$ZodString` constructor definitions in `apps/console/dist/assets/*.js`.

| build | zod version literals | `$ZodString` defs |
|---|---|---|
| base, injected | 2: `4.6.1` (vendor-objectstack) + `4.6.5` (vendor-zod) | 2 |
| base + `zod` in `resolve.dedupe`, injected | 2, byte-identical to the row above | 2 |
| this PR, injected | 1: `4.6.5` | 1 |
| this PR, plain (no override) | 1: `4.6.5` | 1 |

With the fix, the injected build's chunk layout matches the plain build's: zod sits in `vendor-objectstack` and there is no separate `vendor-zod` chunk. Only the second copy produced that chunk.

## Verification (all at HEAD `e95a18845` unless noted)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the touched test file plus the 14 other script and console test files that read the console Vite config: **15 files, 860 tests passed**, exit 0. Files: `vite-objectstack-spec-dist`, `vite-objectstack-client-dist`, `check-eager-closure-budget`, `console-vite-alias-closure-4925`, `scripts-type-check`, `side-effects-declaration-consistency`, `vite-declared-lazy-views`, `vite-ineffective-dynamic-imports`, `vite-types-zod-lazy`, `vitest-config-alias-targets-3944`, `vitest-config-type-check`, `check-changeset-presence`, `cross-file-line-citation-census`, `StudioRoute`, `SetupRoute`.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts`: exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` confirms both the module and its test are in that program.
- `pnpm type-check:vitest-config` (`tsc -b apps/console/tsconfig.node.json --force`, which covers `vite.config.ts`): exit 0.
- Console `vite build`, plain and injected: both exit 0, one zod each (table above).
- eslint on the three touched files: 0 errors. The test file has 5 warnings, the same 5 `no-explicit-any` it has at base.
  - Population: the repo-root flat config; JSON output covers 3 files, none ignored.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions` / `project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.
- Light gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:pre-install-import-graph`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check-changeset-presence` ("no changeset is owed": no published source or contract changed), and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED).
- Declared to CI, not run locally: full `pnpm test`, the turbo `pnpm lint`, the console app-source `tsc --noEmit`, and e2e.

### Reverse verification (each leg through `ablation-replace.mjs`, after commit; each restored with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Every leg was predicted plain RED.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | redirect unregistered in `vite.config.ts`, injected console build | build exit 1, guard: "carries 2 zod instances" naming `zod 4.6.1` at the framework store and `zod 4.6.5` at objectui's |
| A2 | parity call removed | 3 red: refuses-older-zod, peerDependencies, config-anchored parity |
| A3 | guard threshold raised from "more than 1" to "more than 99" copies | 2 red: two-copy build, same-version twin |
| A4 | `enforce: 'pre'` removed | 2 red: redirect build (Vite's resolver answers first), config wiring |
| A5 | counter-probe disabled | 1 red: no-zod build |

### End to end, with the real injection (measured at `1ffe5fe77`; the later commits change only comments and the guard's message text)

- **Node probe through the console's own resolution.** It bundles the real metadata-admin `getPackageSchema` / `getDashboardSchema` / `getReportSchema` / `getPageSchema` / `getListVariantSchema` / `getListColumnSchema`, using the live config's alias table and its `singleZodPlugin`, then runs the result in node.
  - With the redirect: 1 zod directory (4.6.5), and all six schemas derived (property counts 25 / 21 / 21 / 24 / 50 / 14) with no `[...-schema]` warnings. The package schema has `name`, `id` and `namespace`.
  - Control without the redirect: 2 zod directories (4.6.5 + 4.6.1). It still derives all six, because zod 4.6.5 happens to walk 4.6.1's schemas. At the reported pin (4.4.3) that same walk threw.
  - So at today's `main` the split is latent: two instances that agree. Under this PR, the 4.4.3 shape is refused at build time by the parity check (pinned in the tests) instead of shipping.
- **Browser (Chromium).** I served the injected build with `vite preview` on port 5371, with `/api` proxied to an isolated `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh -p 4371` of framework `examples/app-crm`. Nothing was written to `packages/console/dist` or `.cache`, the app-crm tree has no residual files, and both servers were stopped by PID.
  - Studio, "New package (writable base)": the dialog rendered `mdf-name`, `mdf-id`, `mdf-namespace`, `mdf-version`, `mdf-type` and `mdf-description` with the spec-derived help text. Create was enabled, `POST /api/v1/packages` answered **201**, and the package was listed as Writable.
  - CRM `pipeline_dashboard` inspector: rendered spec-derived Layout fields (Columns / Gap / Refresh Interval Seconds) and 0 "Spec schema unavailable" banners.
  - 0 `[...-schema]` console messages. The only zod-bearing vendor chunk loaded was `vendor-objectstack-DjMuOTNe.js`.
  - Not driven in the browser: a report surface, because app-crm has no report. It is covered by the node probe above.
- Not measured: the dev server (`vite` serve) with the override set. The redirect also registers there, but only builds were measured.

## Acceptance notes

- **Framework follow-up (objectstack-ai/objectstack, NOT in this PR):**
  - Bump `.objectui-sha` to a commit that contains this PR. At the current pin `db11afd4967c` the console's zod is 4.4.3, and with this PR the parity check would correctly refuse the build against spec `^4.6.1`.
  - Add a single-zod canary to `scripts/build-console.sh`, for example by counting distinct zod version literals in `assets/*.js`. The in-build guard already fails the build, so the canary is belt-and-braces.
  - Add the spec's zod (or the spec manifest) to the `release.yml` console cache key, which today keys only on `.objectui-sha` and the script.
- Pre-registered siblings objectui#11070 and objectui#10859 (`packages/types/src/zod/**`): this PR moves **no** workspace zod version and **no** lockfile entry. The new guard will fail any console build where objectui's own lockfile resolves zod twice.
- `zod` is intentionally absent from `resolve.dedupe` (see above). A comment there points at the redirect and the guard.
- Environment deviation: this container runs Node 22.22.0, and jsdom 30 declares `^22.22.2`. `engine-strict=true` refused `pnpm install`, so I installed with `--config.engine-strict=false`. CI uses its own Node.
